---
title: "One plot, three brands"
description: "theme_brand() reads a brand.yml file, the format behind Quarto's _brand.yml, and turns its colours, palette and fonts into a plot theme. The same code, three brands, and a switch that brands every plot in a document."
categories: [Basics, Text]
image: figs/brand-ledger.png
---



A [brand.yml](https://posit-dev.github.io/brand-yml/) file describes an
organisation's look in one place: its colours, a named palette and its fonts.
Quarto reads it from `_brand.yml` to style a whole website or report.
`theme_brand()` reads the same file and gives a plot the same look, so the
figures match the page around them.

This is one of the three brand files used on this page:


::: {.cell}

```
#> meta:
#>   name: Ledger
#> color:
#>   palette:
#>     oxblood: "#8c2f39"
#>     slate: "#4a6378"
#>     olive: "#6b7d3a"
#>     ink: "#2b2118"
#>   foreground: ink
#>   background: "#f7f1e5"
#>   primary: oxblood
#> typography:
#>   fonts:
#>     - family: Lato
#>       source: google
#>     - family: Playfair Display
#>       source: google
#>   base:
#>     family: Lato
#>     weight: 300
#>   headings:
#>     family: Playfair Display
#>     weight: 700
```
:::


The plot is written once, with no colours and no theme:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pen <- datasets::penguins
pen <- pen[complete.cases(pen), ]

p <- vplot(pen, width = 7.5, height = 4.4) |>
  mark_point(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, color = species,
             size = 2, alpha = 0.75) |>
  mark_smooth(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, color = species,
              method = "lm", se = FALSE) |>
  labs(
    title = "Bigger flippers, heavier penguins",
    subtitle = "Palmer Station, Antarctica, 2007 to 2009",
    x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Body mass (g)", color = NULL,
    caption = "Data: palmerpenguins"
  )
```
:::


Then `theme_brand()` applies a brand. `fetch_fonts = TRUE` downloads the
brand's Google fonts for the session, so the figure is drawn in the right
typeface even on a machine that doesn't have it installed.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p |> theme_brand("brands/ledger.yml", fetch_fonts = TRUE)
```

How the parts of the brand file are used:

- `background` becomes the page and `foreground` the ink of titles, text and
  unmapped marks. The greys of grid lines and tick labels are mixes of the two,
  so they suit any pair of colours.
- `color.palette`, in file order, becomes the default colours for a discrete
  scale. A scale with its own colours still wins.
- `typography.base` sets the text font and `headings` the title font, each at
  its own weight. Ledger asks for light body text (300); tick labels, legend
  text and axis titles keep at least a regular weight so they stay readable at
  small sizes.

## Every plot in a document

In a Quarto project with a `_brand.yml`, one option brands every plot that
does not set a theme of its own. vellumplot reads the brand Quarto has already
resolved for the document, including a dark brand if you ask for one with
`mode = "dark"`, and says once which file it used.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
options(
  vellumplot.brand = TRUE,             # or a path to a brand file
  vellumplot.brand.fetch_fonts = TRUE  # download missing brand fonts
)
```
:::


The option is off by default, and a plot with an explicit theme such as
`theme_bw()` keeps it. A composition with no theme of its own takes its page
from its plots, so branded plots composed side by side share one background.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
counts <- as.data.frame(table(island = pen$island, species = pen$species))
counts <- counts[counts$Freq > 0, ]

bars <- vplot(counts, width = 3.6, height = 4.4) |>
  mark_bar(x = island, y = Freq, fill = species, stat = "identity") |>
  labs(title = "Where they live", x = NULL, y = "Penguins", fill = NULL)

brand <- "brands/midnight.yml"
both <- hconcat(
  theme_brand(p, brand, fetch_fonts = TRUE) |> labs(caption = NULL),
  theme_brand(bars, brand)
)
```
